name: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor
title: EscalationPolicyEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of outlined levels, each a MonarchDurationInput (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField with steppers) and a multiple-choice MonarchEntityPicker (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet), with MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButton
summary: Edits an escalation ladder: at each level, after how long and whom to notify, so an alert or request nobody acts on reaches someone else.
whenToUse: Unacknowledged incidents or overdue approvals must move to other people over time, and each level notifies one or more channels, rotas or people.
whenNotToUse: For approvals that happen in order, use MonarchApprovalChainEditor. For messages sent to customers on a schedule, use a sequence of steps built from MonarchActionEditor.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor(value: List<MonarchEscalationLevel>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchEscalationLevel>) -> Unit, targets: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, timing: MonarchEscalationTiming = MonarchEscalationTiming.Cumulative, description: String? = null, defaultStepMinutes: Int = 15, minLevels: Int = 1, maxLevels: Int = 10, showErrors: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, createId: (() -> String)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels = MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels())

public data class MonarchEscalationLevel(id: String, afterMinutes: Int, targets: List<String> = emptyList()) { companion object { fun validate(levels: List<MonarchEscalationLevel>, timing: MonarchEscalationTiming = MonarchEscalationTiming.Cumulative): Map<String, MonarchEscalationLevelProblem> } }
public enum class MonarchEscalationTiming { Cumulative, Interval }
public enum class MonarchEscalationLevelProblem { Targets, Order }

public class MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels(label: String? = null, level: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, after: String? = null, notify: String? = null, summary: ((duration: String, names: String) -> String)? = null, nobody: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeLevel: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, noTargets: String? = null, targetsProblem: String? = null, orderProblem: String? = null, maxReached: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The levels, in order. Ids must be unique.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after every change.

options.name: targets
options.description: What a level can notify: channels, rotas or people, with an optional description such as the kind.

options.name: timing
options.description: Cumulative measures every time from the start, so levels must get later; Interval measures each from the previous level.

options.name: defaultStepMinutes
options.description: The minutes a new level adds to the last one (cumulative), or its time (interval).

options.name: minLevels
options.description: The fewest levels; the remove buttons are disabled at this count.

options.name: maxLevels
options.description: The most levels; the add button is replaced by a note at this count.

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows the problems of each level, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the policy can be changed.

options.name: createId
options.description: Makes the id of a new level; by default the first free level-<n>.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button; without it the button reads Remove.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before the text of the add button.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each level shows its heading, a summary such as After 15m, notify On-call rota, a remove button, the time field and the target picker.

states.name: no targets
states.description: A warning notice says there is nothing to notify yet.

states.name: invalid
states.description: With showErrors, a level that notifies nobody shows the problem on the picker, and a level not later than the one before shows it on the time field; the level takes the danger outline.

states.name: at the limit
states.description: The add button is replaced by A policy can have up to 10 levels.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every field and button is disabled.

appearance: Each level is an outlined card on the surface color with a subtle border, or the danger border while it shows a problem. Headings are strong body text, summaries muted captions; the fields have the input border and the add button is a small secondary MonarchButton. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same data shape, defaults and checks as the web (validateEscalationPolicy is MonarchEscalationLevel.validate). Targets are MonarchEntityPickerEntity values chosen in a multiple-choice MonarchEntityPicker sheet, where the web lists a checkbox per target; the sheet searches and scales to long lists of people. Problems are shown as the error of the field concerned instead of a paragraph under the level, so TalkBack reads them with that field. The web's numbered marker beside each level is left out: the Level 1 heading carries the number. The web's messages prop is labels. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each level heading (Level 1) is a heading, and each level is a traversal group with its summary, fields and remove button.
The list of levels is named Escalation levels.
Remove buttons are named with the position (Remove level 1) and are 48dp targets.
A problem is the error of the field concerned, read with it and announced when it appears; the danger outline is never the only signal.
The no-targets warning is a MonarchInlineNotice that says its tone.
edgeCases: Clearing the time field stores 1 minute, the minimum, as on the web.
Target ids that are not in targets keep their place at the end of the level and show the id in the summary.
Durations of a day or more show days in the summary, such as 1d 2h.
The editor does not scroll on its own: put it in a scrolling screen.
